label: A rational power is fixed toward a being it gives only if the giver's end requires that being
paraphrase: OPEN (WN, analyst formulation, unattributed): if y gives x being at w by exercising a rational power and is fixed toward x from w (NECESSITATE_5: gives x being at w and at every accessible world where y exists), then x is required by y's own end (EndRequires y x, the teleological means-to-end relation: x is a means without which y's end cannot be attained; x's necessary existence does not make it required). The pinned ST I q.19 a.3 co. supports the narrower case of willing a means as necessitated by willing its end (claim fa4fa750-39a9-4f00-9c30-8b4b90682fab). The application to fixity of giving across accessible worlds remains open. Rivals on which a perfect will is fixed (NECESSITATE_5) toward effects its own good does not require: the necessary diffusion of the good (Neoplatonic emanation; Avicenna's First as standardly reported), Rowe's argument that a perfectly good creator of the best is not free, and Kretzmann's Dionysian argument (navigation). Leibniz's moral necessity of choosing the best is not metaphysical necessity, so it is not a fixity in this sense.
